The `source` and `sha256sums` arrays reference Azul's official CDN with predictable URLs based on version variables, which is expected for this package type. No network operations or file system modifications occur during sourcing. The use of `printf` and `exit` in the `case` block is safe as it only handles unsupported architectures and runs in a predictable control flow. There are no obfuscated expressions or malicious payloads.
</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a package for Azul Zulu JDK with JavaFX, targeting x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. It fetches prebuilt JDK binaries from Azul's official CDN (cdn.azul.com) using HTTPS, which is a trusted source. The package installation routine extracts the JDK into the appropriate directory under `/usr/lib/jvm`, relocates configuration, license, and man page files to standard system locations, and creates symbolic links to maintain proper filesystem hierarchy as expected by Arch Linux Java packaging standards. These operations are confined to the package build environment (`$pkgdir`) and do not affect the host system during build.

All actions are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for JDK distributions. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network activity, or execution of downloaded content beyond extraction. The use of symbolic links for shared resources (conf, legal, man) is normal and safe. No dangerous commands such as `eval`, `curl|bash`, or remote code execution patterns are present.

LLM auditresponse for zulu-jdk-fx.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `zulu-jdk-fx.install` script is a standard Arch Linux package hook used to manage Java alternatives via the `archlinux-java` utility. It defines post-install, post-upgrade, and pre-remove actions to properly register or unregister the Zulu JDK FX as the default Java implementation when the package is installed, updated, or removed.

The script uses a helper function `_fix_default` to check the current default Java VM by calling `/usr/bin/archlinux-java get`. If no default is set (i.e., `/usr/bin/java` is not executable), it unsets any default to ensure consistency. During installation and upgrade, if no default Java is set, it sets the current Zulu FX JDK as the default. On removal, it unsets the default only if the removed package was the current default. All operations are confined to the system's Java alternative system and do not perform network operations, execute external untrusted code, or manipulate files outside their scope.

These are standard, expected behaviors for a JVM package in AUR. The script does not contain obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized file access. It interacts solely with the `archlinux-java` tool, which is part of the base system's Java management framework. No malicious or suspicious activity is present.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard Java alternative management, no malicious behavior
</summary>
</security_assessment>
